title: MTEL Physical Education (22) Practice Test - MTEL - Rhythmic Movement and Dance
subject: MTEL

questions.q: A student who claps twice in an even rhythm to each beat of a four-beat measure of music is marking the:
questions.explain: In a four-beat measure, each beat is typically a quarter note. Clapping twice evenly for each beat means dividing each quarter note into two equal parts, which are eighth notes.

questions.q: To introduce students to the rhythmic use of locomotor skills, it would be more appropriate to design patterns that include hopping rather than patterns that include skipping because hopping:
options: is a quieter, more controlled movement than skipping.
can be done in any direction, while skipping can move only in the direction of the leading foot.
involves one count and skipping involves two counts.
is more likely than skipping to be included as a movement in various dance forms.
questions.explain: Hopping is a simpler rhythmic movement because it takes place on a single beat or count. Skipping is more complex, involving a step and a hop in an uneven two-part rhythm. Starting with hopping helps students first master moving with the beat.

questions.q: Before introducing students to the basic steps used in an ethnic social dance, a teacher shows them a video of a performance featuring the dance that begins with a narrator outlining the story the dancers perform. The narration will most likely enhance students' understanding of dance as:
options: an important part of theatrical productions.
questions.explain: By explaining the story behind the dance, the narration helps students understand a key concept: that dance is a form of communication and that choreographed movements can be used to convey meaning and tell stories.
